alumniModel.label: modeled
notes: Official earnings line is College Scorecard median 10 years after entry (College Transitions compilation of Scorecard, Dec 2025). We treat Opportunity Insights (Chetty) mid-career earnings as the other official lane but did not ingest OI tables in v1.
We do not invent a silent point-estimate of alumni net worth. Stock is shown only as a modeled range.
Cohort sketch: undergrad enrollment proxy × 35-year working-alumni window × 0.72 completion × 0.88 still-living/reachable.
Wealth-to-income: low = 5× (SCF-like median path, college-educated ages ~45–54); high = 12× (mean path plus a top-1% bump). Not SCF microdata.
Annual giving flow = 0.5% of low wealth to 2% of high wealth (all-cause). A modeled 4% athletics-directed slice of that flow is what enters capacity after subtracting booked athletic contributions.
Capacity is an ANNUAL FLOW, not a wealth stock.

conferenceExit.label: Conference exit
conferenceExit.source: 2023–24 SEC Bylaws, §3.2 Withdrawal Fee (hosted PDF)

fee.source: 2023–24 SEC Bylaws, §3.2 Withdrawal Fee (hosted PDF)
fee.notes: With required notice. Headline cell.

conferenceExit.notes: Bylaw withdrawal fee — cash to the conference. The bylaws do not say a departing school leaves with media rights. Not equivalent to the ACC settlement ladder. School-page cell is §3.2.1 with-notice ($30 million). §3.2.2 $40 million without notice and §3.2.3 $45 million if deemed withdrawn are footnoted, not booked as the headline. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity.

capacity.fiscalYearNote: Most complete public category stack is Knight-Newhouse / CNBC FY2024. FY2025 SEC distribution is a phase-in, not a full media share.

mediaConference.source: Knight-Newhouse via CNBC Official College Sports Valuations 2025 (conference/NCAA/media/postseason)
mediaConference.notes: Texas SEC phase-in FY2025 was $12.1M (CBS/AP). We keep the more complete FY2024 media/conference stack so capacity is not understated by the one-year phase-in.

secPhaseIn.source: SEC / CBS Sports / Dallas Morning News — Texas FY2025 conference distribution (phase-in)
secPhaseIn.notes: Not added on top of FY2024 media/conference. Shown as a gap/phase-in marker.

sponsorships.source: Knight-Newhouse via CNBC — corporate sponsorship, advertising, licensing

tickets.source: Sportico — Texas football ticket sales FY2025 (highest-category public figure we could verify quickly). Full all-sport tickets were $60.91M in FY2024 KN.
tickets.notes: Football tickets only for FY2025. All-sport FY2024 was $60.91M (KN/CNBC).

contributions.source: Knight-Newhouse via CNBC — donor contributions

studentFees.source: Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database — FY2025 NCAA MFRS student fees (line 3)
studentFees.notes: Cited $0 on KN FY2025 MFRS line 3 — not an invented blank.

institutionalSupport.source: Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database — FY2025 NCAA MFRS institutional/government support (lines 2+4+6+6A combined)
institutionalSupport.notes: Cited $0 on KN FY2025 institutional/government support — not an invented blank.

governmentSupport.source: Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database — FY2025 institutional/government support is $0, so the government slice is $0
governmentSupport.notes: KN combined allocated-support line is $0, so Line 2 government support is $0.

capacity.subsidyNotes: KN FY2025 MFRS allocated-revenue lines are $0 — cited self-supporting on student fees and institutional/government support, not an invented blank. EADA 2024–25 has no split to contradict this.

undergradEnrollment.source: Rounded IPEDS-ish undergraduate headcount proxy (College Grad Analyst / College Navigator scale)
undergradEnrollment.notes: Used only as a cohort-size proxy. Not a census of living alumni.

officialEarnings.source: College Scorecard median earnings 10 years after entry, compiled by College Transitions (Dec 2025)
officialEarnings.notes: Official alumni earnings line. Scorecard, not a net-worth figure. Opportunity Insights (Chetty) mid-career earnings are the other official lane; we did not scrape the OI microdata in v1.

booked.source: Texas Public Radio / Houston Public Media — UT-Austin disclosed $13.5M revenue-share payments Jul 2025–end Mar 2026
booked.notes: School disclosure of House Year 1 year-to-date spend. On-track ~$18M is a projection — not booked. Do not add the FY2025 $3.2M MFRS line below (Jul–Aug 2025 overlaps this window). Do not book the $18M cap plan.

preCap.source: Austin American-Statesman — Texas FY2025 NCAA financial report: $3.2M revenue-sharing (year ended Aug 31, 2025)
preCap.notes: School FY ends Aug 31, so this MFRS line is only two months of House (Jul 1–Aug 31, 2025). Not the $18M cap plan (Del Conte / Novak). Included in the House Year 1 YTD $13.5M above — not additional.

collective990.source: IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc (EIN 87-3873183), calendar 2022, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Schedule O / Part IX line 11g: Student athlete contractors $423,157.
collective990.line: Part IX line 11g — Student athlete contractors
collective990.notes: Collective 990 — third-party exempt filing, lagged. Not a House spent total, not Item 44, not a player contract. Not added to booked NIL, pre-cap, capacity, or the booked-only rank. 501(c)(3). Calendar-year return filed Nov. 15, 2023.

collective990.source: IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc (EIN 87-3873183), calendar 2023, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Schedule O / Part IX line 11g: Student athlete appearances $11,717,673.
collective990.line: Part IX line 11g — Student athlete appearances
collective990.notes: Collective 990 — third-party exempt filing, lagged. Not a House spent total, not Item 44, not a player contract. Not added to booked NIL, pre-cap, capacity, or the booked-only rank. 501(c)(3). Calendar-year return filed Nov. 19, 2024. Other Part IX 11g rows (Clark Field, contract/professional fees) are not athlete pay and are not booked here.

collective990.source: IRS Form 990 — Texas One Fund Inc (EIN 87-3873183), calendar 2024, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Schedule O / Part IX line 11g: Student athlete appearances $14,540,650.
collective990.line: Part IX line 11g — Student athlete appearances
collective990.notes: Collective 990 — third-party exempt filing, lagged. Not a House spent total, not Item 44, not a player contract. Not added to booked NIL, pre-cap, capacity, or the booked-only rank. 501(c)(3). Calendar-year return in the IRS 2025 TEOS XML release (object 202503359349301145).

houseRemaining.source: House Year 1 remaining = published $20.5M NCAA House cap minus this school’s booked House spent cell
houseRemaining.notes: Published House Year 1 cap minus booked House spent. Residual, not a filing. Year-to-date window — not a full-year leftover.
houseRemaining.footnote: House Year 1 remaining as of YTD (Jul 2025–Mar 2026) = $20.5M cap − $13.5M booked. Partial-year, not a full-year leftover. The $3.2M pre-cap / MFRS line is inside the $13.5M — not added. Collective 990s are not in this math.

conferenceExit.label: Conference exit
conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.
grantOfRights.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

distribution.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

fee.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file
fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (University of Arizona) 38,009,311 × 2 = 76,018,622. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. conferenceExit.label: Conference exit
conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.
grantOfRights.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

distribution.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

fee.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file
fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (Arizona State University) 43,009,550 × 2 = 86,019,100. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. FY2025 was a half-share year for BYU / Houston / UCF / Cincinnati; FY2026 is their first full-share year. We do not silently 2× the half-share as if that is the going-forward buyout. Headline is a modeled range from named full-share peers on the same 990 (2 × $37,879,865–$43,009,550). Last filed FY2025 half-share (Brigham Young University) 23,110,622 × 2 = 46,221,244 — shown as a footnote only, not the headline.

conferenceExit.label: Conference exit
conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.
grantOfRights.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

distribution.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

fee.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file
fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. FY2025 was a half-share year for BYU / Houston / UCF / Cincinnati; FY2026 is their first full-share year. We do not silently 2× the half-share as if that is the going-forward buyout. Headline is a modeled range from named full-share peers on the same 990 (2 × $37,879,865–$43,009,550). Last filed FY2025 half-share (University of Cincinnati) 20,211,539 × 2 = 40,423,078 — shown as a footnote only, not the headline.

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.
grantOfRights.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

fee.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file
fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (University of Colorado) 39,034,422 × 2 = 78,068,844. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.

fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.
grantOfRights.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (Kansas State University) 39,830,544 × 2 = 79,661,088. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.

fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (Oklahoma State University) 38,038,756 × 2 = 76,077,512. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.

fee.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file
fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (Texas Christian University) 39,272,007 × 2 = 78,544,014. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.

conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.

fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. conferenceExit.source: Big 12 Conference Inc. FY2025 Form 990, Schedule I grantee list (year ended June 2025) — Plinth extract of IRS e-file

formula.text: Any Withdrawing Member shall pay to the Conference a commitment buyout fee (the “Buyout Amount”) in an amount equal to the sum of the amount of distributions that otherwise would be paid to the Member during the final two years of its membership in the Conference.
formula.source: Big 12 Conference Bylaws, §3.4 Buyout Amount and §3.1 Grant of Rights (hosted PDF)

grantOfRights.text: the Withdrawal of a Member and the payment of the Buyout Amount and implementation of the provisions of these Bylaws does not abrogate the obligations of such Withdrawing Member pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Grant of Rights Agreement
grantOfRights.plain: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow.

fee.notes: Paying the 2×-distributions cash formula does not buy back media rights. The grant of rights still sits with the league. This is a cash fee only — not the ACC settlement ladder, which lets a school leave with rights in tow. Hosted Big 12 bylaws §3.4: Buyout Amount = the sum of distributions that otherwise would be paid during the final two years of membership. Modeled here as 2 × the last cited FY2025 Form 990 Schedule I distribution — a labeled model, not a booked invoice. The hosted PDF still lists old members; we cite the withdrawal section, not the stale roster. Not a coach-firing buyout. Not part of annual capacity. Named FY2025 Schedule I line (West Virginia University) 39,582,600 × 2 = 79,165,200. Labeled modeled — the bylaw looks forward two membership years; this is last filed × 2, not an invoice.
